title: Celestin's repertoire and the arranger Caesar
summary: Celestin played mostly stock arrangements. Caesar arranged "Ring Them Bells".

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: All kinds of numbers. He played mostly stock arrangements. He had a lot of other arrangements too.
Well who was the one who arranged Ring Them Bells? I get all this mixed up now. You told me before. Cesar. Cesar? Yeah. Ring Them Bells. The saxophone player from St. Louis?
Thornton or Thompson or something like that.

I don't know his first name, but I know it's Cesar. He's a pretty good arranger. You never arranged anything yourself, huh? One number. And that was when I was with Willie O'Connor. He recorded. He was playing with Joe Robichard at the time. I found a new baby. Who? He was playing with Joe Robichard at the time. What was the number? I found a new baby. No. I mean, Joe Robichard records. He was playing with Joe Robichard's record. I don't think I've ever heard Joe Robichard's record of that. Joe Robichard recorded for Decca and they never put them out. Well, see, how I know you recorded, Willie O'Connor, did you know, he was playing with Joe Robichard's record of that. I don't think I've ever heard Joe Robichard's record of that.
